questions.question: What is a key structural difference between CommonJS's `require()` and ES Modules' `import`?
options: They are functionally identical, just different syntax
require() is dynamic and can be called conditionally anywhere in code; import statements are static and resolved before any code runs
import only works in the browser, never in Node.js
require() cannot export more than one value
questions.explanation: import declarations are hoisted and statically analyzable at the top of a file, while require() is a normal function call that can appear anywhere, including inside conditionals.

questions.question: What is the main practical difference between a named export and a default export when importing?
options: Named exports can be imported under any local name; default exports must match exactly
Default exports can be imported under any local name since there's no name to match; named exports must match (or be explicitly renamed with `as`)
A module can have unlimited default exports
questions.explanation: A default export has no fixed name, so the importer can call it anything; named exports are matched by their exported name unless aliased.

questions.question: What does tree-shaking do?
options: It removes exported code that is never actually imported/used anywhere, shrinking the final bundle
It converts ES Modules into CommonJS
questions.explanation: Tree-shaking analyzes the import graph and strips out unused exports from the final bundle.

questions.question: Why does tree-shaking work reliably with ES Modules but not with CommonJS?
options: CommonJS doesn't support exports at all
ES Module imports/exports are static, top-level, and analyzable without running code; CommonJS's require() can be dynamic/conditional, which defeats static analysis
Tree-shaking actually works equally well with both
Bundlers refuse to process CommonJS files entirely
questions.explanation: Static analysis needs to know exactly what's imported from where without executing anything — ES Modules guarantee this structurally, while CommonJS's dynamic require() calls don't.
